target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a Seed-stage company operating in the Ocean & Maritime sector. Founded by Sam Mendel, a serial founder with a prior marketplace exit, and Eric Kim, former Palantir and Merge engineer, the company has raised $1M to date. The comp universe consists of three private peers in the same sector (Standard Subsea, Clippership, Albacore); no public maritime-tech comparables were identified.

Given the early stage and limited methodological inputs, only the Stage-Progression approach is applicable. This method uses the $1M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A step-ups, yielding an implied valuation of $2M. This single triangulation method establishes the foundation for the range estimate.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.0M (low) to $3.0M (high), with a median of $2.0M. This range reflects the typical step-up between Seed and early institutional rounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of public comparables and the small private peer set, which limits benchmarking precision. Additionally, the actual terms and timing of the $1M raise are not specified, introducing ambiguity around whether it should serve as a direct valuation proxy. Founder pedigree and CTO technical depth provide some differentiation within the frontier-tech sector, but revenue, product-market progress, or burn metrics are not provided and would refine this estimate materially.
